title: Add prefetch invocation trajectory metrics and Token Energy Explorer dashboard
author: Leah Park
description: Motivation: Long-tail latency and token-cost variance are often driven by prefetch behavior and kernel warmup effects that are opaque in our current telemetry. This PR instruments a lightweight prefetch trajectory metric set and surfaces an interactive dashboard (Token Energy Explorer) to help SREs and ML platform engineers triage warmup-driven cost spikes and prefetch inefficiencies. Summary: - Add time-series metrics that capture prefetch decision lifecycle: prefetch_request{route,model,tenant}, prefetch_outcome{hit|miss|evicted}, prefetch_latency_ms, prefetch_kv_warm_fraction and a derived token_energy_estimate gauge that approximates per-invocation energy/cost contribution from prefetch activity. - Emit compact OTLP span annotations for kernel-warmup phases (warmup_start, kernel_bind, first_invoke) so traces tie to prefetch metrics. - New Grafana dashboard: Token Energy Explorer with multidimensional heatmap (prefetch hit-rate vs token energy), per-route prefetch trajectory panels, and an execution-path waterfall that links span IDs to the heatmap. - Add an adaptive alert recipe that suppresses noisy prefetch alerts by looking at prefetch_kv_warm_fraction and recent warmup span density. - Tests: unit tests for metric emissions, a small e2e integration that replays synthetic invocations to validate dashboard panels and alert behavior. Rollout plan: feature-flagged telemetry emitted behind runtime flag obs.prefetch_trajectory; staged rollout to dedicated pools for 48h, evaluate false positive rate on alerts, then enable global export. Linear: ENG-2481 tracked metric schema and dashboard design; ENG-2509 tracked alert recipe and rollout steps.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Please add a short explanation in docs for how token_energy_estimate is derived (units and assumptions). Also, can we avoid adding high-cardinality tags to prefetch_request?

Leah Park: Added a detailed derivation section in docs/prefetch-metrics.md and limited request tags to route/model/tenant (no raw prompt hashes). token_energy_estimate is expressed as 'nanojoules-equivalent' derived from kernel cycles and queued token counts; noted assumptions explicitly.
Arjun Patel: The OTLP span enrichment looks good but the warmup_start annotation may be emitted too often. Can we debounce span annotations to reduce cardinality?
Leah Park: Debounce added (200ms local window) and backed by defensive guardrails in span_enricher.go to drop duplicate warmup markers per-invocation. Added unit tests to validate dedupe behavior.
Rina Kaur: Alert tuning: thresholds look aggressive for low-traffic tenants. Suggest adaptive threshold that scales with recent invocation volume.
Leah Park: Implemented alert recipe to use rolling 1h invocation count as a gating signal; low volume tenants are auto-muted for prefetch alerts. Updated rollout notes to monitor mute-rate.
Miguel Santos: CI flake on dashboard lint during first run; reran CI and all checks passed. Approving after green CI.
Arjun Patel: Approving — small nits addressed. Ready to squash-merge once runbook links are added.
Leah Park: Added runbook snippet and deep-links in docs. Marking ready for merge.
ci_summary: Initial CI: lint failure on dashboard schema (missing panel description) -> fixed -> re-run -> all checks pass (unit, integration, dashboard-lint, license-check).
release_notes: Added prefetch trajectory metrics and Token Energy Explorer dashboard. New telemetry behind feature flag obs.prefetch_trajectory. Enables tracing of kernel warmup phases and reduces noisy prefetch alerts with adaptive gating.
notes_for_ops: Feature off by default. To enable set runtime flag obs.prefetch_trajectory=true on a small dedicated pool and monitor metric prefetch_outcome and token_energy_estimate for 48h. Suggested alerting guardrails included in docs/observability/prefetch-metrics.md. If noise increases, rollback by disabling flag.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover metric payload encoding and span dedupe logic. e2e test replays a synthetic 1k-invocation trace with jitter to validate heatmap generation. CI includes dashboard linting step to prevent panel schema regressions.
